# At most, two two-limb numbers

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/Statements.v, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `le_2_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether $x \le y$, for the exact values:

$$m = [\, x \le y \,].$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $y = y_0 + y_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x <= y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `bool` |  |
| `y >= x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `bool` |  |
| `x <= y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `bool` | the `Expansion<T, 1>` operand is converted to two limbs first, exactly |
| `x <= y` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `bool` | the `Expansion<T, 1>` operand is converted to two limbs first, exactly |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.
- $y$ is normalized: $y_0 = \mathrm{RN}(y_0 + y_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $m$ is true exactly when $x \le y$, for the exact values.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit and any exponent range, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `le_2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Compare.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Compare.v), against `le_2_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition le_2_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 y0 y1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec y0 y1 ->
  let m := le_2_2 x0 x1 y0 y1 in
  m = Rle_bool (x0 + x1) (y0 + y1).
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** limbs compared in order (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/le_2_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/le_2_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`, rounded to nearest; `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# x <= y for 2-limb numbers, comparing the limbs in order.

h = lt(x0, y0)
e = eq(x0, y0)
l = le(x1, y1)
t = and(e, l)
m = or(h, t)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#le_2_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 65 600 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 65 600 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 18 118 326 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
